newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end lower, bank shares recover.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end lower, bank shares recover.

text.p: Singapore stock market ended weaker on Tuesday but bank shares recovered from a sell-off prompted by fears of exposure in Thailand's bank crisis.
Foreign tranches of UOB and OUB rose S$0.30-0.40.
"Yesterday's sell-off was an over-reaction. At this point of time, we don't have enough information on the banks' exposure in Thailand," said one dealer.

"In terms of 1996 earnings, banks will not disappoint," said Chen Young Mee, deputy director of research at Vickers Ballas Investment Research. "Looking ahead the (Singapore) economy is expected to pick up and that's positive."
"All the banks are looking for growth in the region like Malaysia, Hong Kong and Australia. We still like the banks with significant overseas contribution," Chen said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 6.90 points down at 2,189.44. Total market volume was 310.9 million units with 354 losers against 62 gainers.

Nervousness following death of Malaysia tycoon Yahaya Ahmad of Proton triggered heavy profit-taking and selling of Malaysian shares traded over the counter. The UOB OTC index fell 20.46 points to 1,313.43. Fruit seller FHTK saw more than 20 million shares traded on punters' interest.
